latest_nl_proof: Let x be any real number, and set m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m is an integer satisfying m <= x < m + 1. Subtracting m throughout gives 0 <= x - m < 1. By the definition of the fractional part, frac(x) = x - floor(x) = x - m. Hence 0 <= frac(x) < 1. Also, rearranging the identity frac(x) = x - floor(x) yields x = floor(x) + frac(x). Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
role_in_parent: Provide the canonical decomposition of an arbitrary real number into an integer part and a fractional part.
statement_nl: For every real number x, x = floor(x) + frac(x), and 0 <= frac(x) < 1.

domain_restrictions: frac(x) is constrained by inequality 0 <= frac(x) < 1
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every real number x, define n = floor(x) and f = frac(x). Then x = n + f and the fractional part satisfies 0 <= f and f < 1.
